extracted.intended_audience: editors, literary scholars, and general readers of Edmund Burke; those preparing or evaluating scholarly editions of historical works
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and evaluating a scholarly edition of a deceased author's works: decisions about selection, ordering, emendation, orthography, referencing, and preserving/authenticating authorial material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful following of prior authoritative edition
rubrics_metrics.description: Such errors of the press as have been discovered in it are here rectified: in other respects it is faithfully followed...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an earlier authoritative edition as the foundation; correct discovered press errors but otherwise preserve the established text unless there is clear reason to deviate (minor, expressly noted exceptions permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological arrangement of works
rubrics_metrics.description: They are disposed in chronological order...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange pieces in (strict) chronological order when possible to preserve the historical sequence; minor deviations only for compelling reasons (e.g., to place a newly discovered piece in its proper context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert important discovered pieces in their proper place
rubrics_metrics.description: a speech of conspicuous excellence... is here, for the first time, inserted in its proper place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When previously omitted but significant pieces are found, include them and place them where they belong chronologically/contextually rather than leaving them omitted or segregated without explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit temporary or ephemeral prefaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The several posthumous publications... were accompanied by appropriate prefaces. These, however, as they were principally intended for temporary purposes, have been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude transient, purpose-specific prefatory material that was not intended for lasting inclusion, while retaining only those explanations necessary for current readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the author's own corrections and corrected copies
rubrics_metrics.description: From this, which was found preserved with his other papers, his friends afterwards thought it their duty to give an authentic edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give priority to manuscripts, pamphlets, or copies that the author personally corrected when reconstructing authoritative text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not attribute to the author sentiments not explicitly known
rubrics_metrics.description: care has been taken not to attribute to Mr. Burke any sentiment which is not most explicitly known, from repeated conversations, and from much correspondence, to have been decidedly entertained by that illustrious man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ascribing opinions or wording to the author unless there is clear documentary evidence (letters, recorded conversations, corrected manuscripts). Be conservative in attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use external reports/documents as evidence cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: the reports of the different committees... amply furnished him with evidence for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the author relied on external official documents, those may be used to complete or contextualize the work, but editors must note limits and avoid overreaching beyond what the evidence supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve meaning when reconstructing imperfect manuscripts; exercise limited discretion only in subordinate points
rubrics_metrics.description: No important change, none at all affecting the meaning of any passage, has been made in either, though in the more imperfect parcel some latitude of discretion in subordinate points was necessarily used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filling gaps or ordering fragmented material, refrain from altering the author's intended meaning; any editorial discretionary changes should be confined to minor, subordinate matters and be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select only tracts fit for inclusion in the collected edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The tracts, most of them in manuscript, which have been already selected as fit for this purpose, will probably furnish four or five volumes more...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate supplementary material: select tracts and manuscripts judged appropriate for the edition rather than indiscriminately publishing every surviving fragment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance contents for methodical volume arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: A different distribution of the contents... has, at the same time, been fortunately found to produce a more methodical arrangement of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute material across volumes to balance bulk and produce a more logical, methodical grouping of works (chronology, genre, or theme).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct and reconcile confused references and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Appendix to the Speech on the Nabob of Arcot's Debts the references were found to be confused, and, in many places, erroneous... The text and the documents that support it have throughout been accommodated to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appendices, notes, and documentary references accurately correspond to the main text; correct reference errors and harmonize supporting materials with the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize orthography using the author's consistent practice; otherwise follow best authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The orthography has been in many cases altered, and an attempt made to reduce it to some certain standard. The rule laid down for the discharge of this task was, that, whenever Mr. Burke could be perceived to have been uniform in his mode of spelling, that was considered as decisive; but where he varied... the best received authorities were directed to be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modernizing or standardizing spelling, preserve the author's own consistent spellings where identifiable; where the author varies, adopt widely accepted editorial/authority standards and document changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare quotations with original sources and correct misquotations
rubrics_metrics.description: The quotations which are interspersed through the works of Mr Burke, and which were frequently made by him from memory, have been generally compared with the original authors. Several mistakes in printing, of one word for another, by which the sense was either perverted or obscured, are now rectified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify quoted material against original sources and correct transcription or printing errors that alter sense; document emendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include author's marginal notes when meaning is clear; avoid over-interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Several other parts... were indicated in the same manner; but, as they in general consist of single sentences, and as the meaning of the mark by which they were distinguished was not actually expressed, it has not been thought necessary to notice them particularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate marginalia or marks when their intent is clear (e.g., authorial initials), but do not speculate or expand upon ambiguous marks—note them without over-interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate small insertions from copies corrected by the author
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or three small insertions have also been made from a quarto copy corrected by Mr. Burke himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt brief additions or corrections found in author-corrected copies when they improve accuracy and are clearly authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve authenticity when dealing with surreptitious or leaked publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Observations on the Conduct of the Minority'... crept surreptitiously into the world... The friends of the author, without waiting to consult him, instantly obtained an injunction... From this... corrected one of the pamphlets with his own hand. From this... his friends afterwards thought it their duty to give an authentic edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When handling leaked or unauthorized publications, seek injunctions or authoritative copies and reconstruct an authentic text from the author's corrected material where possible; clearly report provenance and irregularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect delicacy/privacy when placing pieces not avowed by the author
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Preface to Brissot's Address,' which having appeared in the author's lifetime, and from delicacy not being avowed by him, did not come within the plan of this edition, but has been placed at the end of the last volume...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a piece was not publicly avowed by the author for reasons of delicacy, editors should place it sensitively (e.g., in supplement) and explain the rationale rather than integrating it uncritically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge gaps and solicit additional materials transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: It is, therefore, once more earnestly requested, that all persons... will have the goodness to transmit, without delay, any notices... in their possession...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about incomplete or missing materials, solicit assistance from readers/archives, and acknowledge editorial limitations in the edition's apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical writing should illuminate morality and support social good
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who searched in them for new discoveries... found the landmarks of science precisely in their former places: and they thought they received but a poor recompense... in seeing every mode of religion attacked... the foundation of every virtue, and of all government, sapped with great art and much ingenuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writings in philosophy ought to illustrate or promote morality, contribute to society and government, and avoid undermining the foundations (religion/virtue/government) without constructive alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using specious, plausible falsehoods that dazzle the imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a sort of gloss upon ingenious falsehoods that dazzles the imagination, but which neither belongs to, nor becomes the sober aspect of truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize sound, conclusive argument over rhetorical plausibility; avoid deploying ingenious but unsubstantial reasoning that may mislead through style rather than substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examining received opinions, proceed with modesty but with freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: we shall consider these institutions with all that modesty with which we ought to conduct ourselves in examining a received opinion; but with all that freedom and candor which we owe to truth...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticize institutions and established views respectfully—maintain humility regarding received wisdom while exercising intellectual freedom to seek truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fill works merely with abuse of reason; ensure substantive purpose or under-plot
rubrics_metrics.description: it had been inexcusable to fill a large volume with the abuse of reason; nor would such an abuse have been tolerable, even for a few pages, if some under-plot, of more consequence than the apparent design, had not been carried on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing material that is largely destructive or merely polemical without a deeper constructive purpose; ensure that critical work serves a larger, substantive aim.
